# OxPHP

> Documentation for OxPHP, a high-performance async PHP application server with built-in TLS, compression, rate limiting, metrics, SSE streaming, and worker mode.

## Getting Started

- [Command-Line Interface](docs/en/getting-started/cli.md): The oxphp binary command grammar — serve the HTTP server, run a single PHP script under CLI semantics, validate configuration, and drop privileges with --user.
- [Docker Guide](docs/en/getting-started/docker.md): Run OxPHP with Docker. Covers minimal and multi-stage Dockerfiles, Compose configuration, PHP ini mounts, health checks, and port reference.
- [Installation](docs/en/getting-started/installation.md): Install OxPHP via Docker image or build from source. Covers prerequisites, verification, and platform notes.
- [Quick Start](docs/en/getting-started/quick-start.md): Get OxPHP running in under 5 minutes. Create a project, write a PHP app, start the server, and make your first request.

## Features

- [Access Logging](docs/en/features/access-logging.md): Structured JSON access logs for every HTTP request in OxPHP, with configurable modes for all requests or errors only.
- [Async Promises](docs/en/features/async-promises.md): Run PHP closures in background threads and await results without blocking the worker pool.
- [Compression](docs/en/features/compression.md): OxPHP compresses responses with Brotli by default, reducing transfer sizes for text, JSON, SVG, and other compressible content types.
- [Custom Error Pages](docs/en/features/error-pages.md): Serve branded HTML error pages for 4xx and 5xx responses in OxPHP, loaded once at startup and served from memory.
- [Decorators](docs/en/features/decorators.md): Intercept PHP function and method calls with attribute-based decorators for logging, timing, caching, and access control.
- [Distributed Tracing & APM](docs/en/features/distributed-tracing.md): W3C Trace Context propagation, OpenTelemetry integration, automatic instrumentation, PHP tracing SDK, and end-to-end observability with OxPHP.
- [Early Response](docs/en/features/early-response.md): Send the HTTP response immediately with oxphp_finish_request() and continue running background tasks in OxPHP.
- [Fiber Multiplexing](docs/en/features/fiber-multiplexing.md): Handle hundreds of concurrent requests on a single PHP worker thread using cooperative multitasking with fibers.
- [Internal Server](docs/en/features/internal-server.md): A dedicated HTTP server for health checks, Prometheus metrics, live configuration, and plugin endpoints.
- [Profiling PHP code](docs/en/features/profiling.md): The definitive practical guide — from first run to production use. Triggers, PHP SDK, attributes, export formats, integration with speedscope/xhgui/pprof, metrics, troubleshooting.
- [Rate Limiting](docs/en/features/rate-limiting.md): Built-in per-IP rate limiting for OxPHP with configurable thresholds, time windows, and standard HTTP rate limit response headers.
- [Request IDs](docs/en/features/request-ids.md): Automatic unique request identifiers in OxPHP for distributed tracing and log correlation across your stack.
- [Routing](docs/en/features/routing.md): Configure OxPHP routing with three modes — traditional file mapping, framework front-controller, and SPA fallback. Each mode mirrors the equivalent nginx try_files directive.
- [Server-Sent Events (SSE)](docs/en/features/sse.md): Stream real-time data to browser clients using Server-Sent Events in OxPHP with built-in backpressure and connection management.
- [Static Files](docs/en/features/static-files.md): OxPHP serves static files with automatic MIME detection, in-memory caching, HTTP cache headers, conditional 304 responses, and Range requests.
- [Timeouts](docs/en/features/timeouts.md): Configure header read timeouts and PHP execution timeouts in OxPHP to protect against slow clients and runaway PHP scripts.
- [TLS](docs/en/features/tls.md): Configure native TLS termination in OxPHP with support for TLS 1.2, TLS 1.3, HTTP/2 ALPN negotiation, and PEM certificates.
- [Worker Mode](docs/en/features/worker-mode.md): Persistent PHP processes that bootstrap once and handle multiple requests, eliminating per-request startup overhead in OxPHP.

## Shared State

- [Migrating Shared\* to an external store](docs/en/shared-state/migrating-to-external-store.md): When to promote in-process Shared\* state to Redis, NATS, or another durable store — the patterns, the semantic gaps, and the concrete migration shape for each Shared\* type.
- [Shared State](docs/en/shared-state/shared-state.md): Process-wide primitives — counters, flags, maps, channels, pools — that let PHP workers coordinate without an external store like Redis or APCu.
- [Shared\* Naming Conventions](docs/en/shared-state/shared-naming.md): Naming conventions for the OxPHP\Shared\* concurrency API — the canonical method vocabulary (get/set, try*/timeout wait policies, is*, fetch*, compareAndSet) that every shared primitive follows.
- [Shared\* Observability](docs/en/shared-state/shared-observability.md): Introspection endpoints, Prometheus metrics, and diagnostic playbooks for the OxPHP\Shared\* primitives — inspect live registry entries, trace reachability graphs, and alert on saturation.
- [Shared\Atomic](docs/en/shared-state/shared-atomic.md): Generic atomic int64 shared across PHP workers — load/store, swap, CAS, fetch-arithmetic and fetch-bitwise with explicit memory-ordering control.
- [Shared\Channel](docs/en/shared-state/shared-channel.md): Bounded MPMC channel shared across PHP workers, with fiber-aware send and recv that return value-typed results for explicit dispatch.
- [Shared\Counter](docs/en/shared-state/shared-counter.md): Atomic int64 accumulator shared across PHP workers — lock-free signed add, atomic exchange, compare-and-set, windowed reset via set(0).
- [Shared\Flag](docs/en/shared-state/shared-flag.md): Atomic boolean shared across PHP workers — kill-switches, circuit breakers, and one-shot markers with lock-free load/store/swap/compareAndSet and explicit memory ordering.
- [Shared\Map](docs/en/shared-state/shared-map.md): Process-wide concurrent hash-map for coordinating state across PHP workers — null-as-absence model, a single linearisable compareAndSet, lazy iteration, and cycle-safe nested Shareable values.
- [Shared\Mutex](docs/en/shared-state/shared-mutex.md): Cross-thread mutual exclusion over a stored value — atomic multi-step updates from PHP workers via withLock / tryWithLock / withLockTimeout with explicit wait policies.
- [Shared\Once](docs/en/shared-state/shared-once.md): Run-once container — exactly one worker's factory produces the value, everyone else sees the memoised result, across the whole OxPHP process.
- [Shared\Pool](docs/en/shared-state/shared-pool.md): Process-wide bounded object pool for expensive per-thread resources — database connections, JSON parsers, HTTP clients — with strict budget, per-thread affinity, and idle-timeout eviction.
- [Shared\Registry](docs/en/shared-state/shared-registry.md): Name-keyed process-global handles for Shared\* primitives — one Map / Counter / Channel that every worker and every request converges on, without external stores.

## Security

- [Dot-Path Blocking](docs/en/security/dot-path-blocking.md): OxPHP blocks access to hidden files and directories (starting with ".") to prevent exposure of sensitive configuration, version control data, and other dotfiles.
- [PHP Execution Deny-List](docs/en/security/php-deny.md): Block PHP execution at specific URI paths to harden legacy applications against uploaded PHP shells and unintended script exposure.
- [Symlink Allow Paths](docs/en/security/symlink-allow-paths.md): Explicit allow-list for symlink targets outside DOCUMENT_ROOT — Laravel-style storage links, shared asset volumes, multi-tenant uploads.
- [Trusted Proxies](docs/en/security/trusted-proxies.md): Configure OxPHP to extract the real client IP, protocol, and host from reverse proxy headers (Forwarded, X-Forwarded-For/Proto/Host).

## PHP

- [HTTP Request API](docs/en/php/request-api.md): Object-oriented API for accessing HTTP request data in OxPHP, replacing PHP superglobals with a type-safe, lazy-loading interface.
- [OPcache and JIT](docs/en/php/opcache.md): Configure OPcache and JIT compilation for optimal PHP performance with OxPHP, including preloading and development settings.
- [PHP Functions](docs/en/php/functions.md): Complete reference for all oxphp_* PHP functions provided by OxPHP, including async, streaming, worker mode, and decorator APIs.
- [Superglobals](docs/en/php/superglobals.md): How OxPHP populates $_SERVER, $_GET, $_POST, $_COOKIE, $_FILES, and php://input for each request.
- [Worker Class](docs/en/php/worker-class.md): Reference for the OxPHP\Server\Worker class — a unified runtime handle for worker introspection, the worker entry point, and per-thread metrics.

## Operations

- [Configuration Reference](docs/en/operations/configuration.md): Complete environment variable reference for OxPHP. Every setting, its default, and what it controls — all in one place.
- [Graceful Shutdown](docs/en/operations/graceful-shutdown.md): How OxPHP handles SIGTERM and SIGINT signals to drain connections and shut down cleanly, with Kubernetes and Docker configuration examples.
- [Health Checks](docs/en/operations/health-checks.md): Internal server endpoints for health monitoring, Kubernetes probes, Prometheus metrics, and runtime configuration inspection.
- [Prometheus Metrics](docs/en/operations/metrics.md): Reference for all Prometheus-compatible metrics exposed by OxPHP at the /metrics endpoint, including request, connection, worker, and compression metrics.

## Architecture

- [Architecture Overview](docs/en/architecture/overview.md): How OxPHP works: async HTTP handling, PHP worker pool, request flow, worker mode, and built-in safety guarantees — from a user's perspective.
